newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer backs $2.70-$3.10 EPS view for FY97.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer backs $2.70-$3.10 EPS view for FY97.

text.p: Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc said Wednesday that it still expects earnings for fiscal 1997 will be between $2.70 and $3.10 a share.
Pioneer earned $2.68 a share in fiscal 1996.
The company said that while the corn planting season is still a few weeks away in most of the United States and Europe, it is on track for "another strong year" in 1997.

Earlier, Pioneer Hi-Bred reported a net loss for the second quarter of $0.02 a share, compared with year-ago income of $0.05 a share. For the first half of fiscal 1997, its net loss was $0.57 a share, compared with a loss of $0.54 a year ago.

Because of the seasonality of the seed business, Pioneer said losses are typical for the first half of the fiscal year. A large portion of the company's sales and profits are generated in the third quarter, ending May 31.

In North America, Pioneer said, hybrid corn seed deliveries during the first half of 1997 were virtually unchanged from a year earlier. Those deliveries are primarily to customers in the southern United States, where corn planting is now underway, it added.
In a statement, Charles Johnson, chairman, said European revenues in the first half of 1997 were reduced by the timing of seed deliveries in Europe and the strength of the U.S. dollar.
However, he added, "our operations in Europe are on track for a strong year in 1997 and results there could exceed the exceptional performance record in 1996."

Outside of Europe and North America, revenues were higher because of continued strength in Asia and stronger results in Mexico. Improved growing conditions and increased economic stability during 1997 have improved the company's prospects in Mexico, it added.
